prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map shows a top-down workspace where the camera wearer's forearms entering from the bottom edge (roughly 0.2 to 0.4 m away) and the protruding box on the upper-left scooter body (0.3 to 0.5 m) are nearest, while the elevated scooter fender and circular brake hub sit at mid-depth (0.5 to 0.7 m) above the receding tiled floor and newspaper (0.8 to 1.0 m). No other people are present, as the camera wearer looks straight down with the scooter frame, brake hub, newspaper, left-side plastic bag, and right-side impact wrench (about 0.3 m right of the hub) all within or just at the edge of arm's reach. Across frames 1 to 5, the camera wearer's hands occlude the lower portion of the hub in frames 1 and 2 before the right arm retreats downward and rightward toward the floor in frames 3 to 5, followed by the left hand pulling back slightly in frame 5 while the scooter partially exits the top and left edges of the frame. Compared to the flat top-down RGB image, the depth map makes the vertical clearance between the suspended scooter assembly and the floor below immediately apparent. However, the map is unreliable for thin or low-profile items on the newspaper—such as the T-handle wrench, screwdriver, and crumpled rags—which blend almost completely into the background floor plane.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map labels the camera wearer's foreground forearms and gloved hands (0.2 to 0.6 m away in the lower center) as 'person' across all five frames, while detecting the upper scooter body and central wheel hub (0.4 to 0.7 m away) as 'motorcycle' only in frame 3 and the tool on the floor to the right (0.8 to 1.0 m away, roughly 0.3 m right of the hub) as 'bottle' in frames 3 and 4. No other people are present in the scene, and the camera wearer faces downward toward the scooter hub within arm's reach while the upper half of the scooter remains truncated by the top and left frame borders. Across the five frames, the segmented arm masks show the two hands together on the hub in frames 1 and 2, separating as the right hand moves down and right in frames 3 and 4, and shifting lower in frame 5. In frame 3, the map helps group the complex mechanical components of the fender, suspension spring, and brake assembly into a single 'motorcycle' silhouette that is visually fragmented in the RGB image. However, segmentation is highly unreliable overall: it misses the motorcycle entirely in four of the five frames, over-extends the frame 3 motorcycle mask onto the newspaper, splits the single camera wearer's left and right arms into separate 'person' instances in frames 3 to 5, and misclassifies the cordless impact wrench as a 'bottle'.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is completely black across all five frames, failing to render any yellow body keypoints or magenta hand joints. From the RGB strip and depth map, no other people are in the scene, and the camera wearer's head-mounted viewpoint is angled straight down at their own two forearms and blue-gloved hands positioned 0.2 to 0.6 m away within immediate arm's reach of the scooter's brake hub. In reality, both hands manipulate the lower edge of the hub in frames 1 and 2 (spaced less than 0.15 m apart) before the right hand retreats roughly 0.2 to 0.3 m downward and rightward in frames 3 to 5 and the left hand withdraws slightly in frame 5. Because only the camera wearer's lower arms enter from the bottom border while their torso, shoulders, and head remain completely out of view behind the camera, the pose map contributes no spatial information beyond what is visible in the RGB frames. The map is entirely unreliable in this sequence due to total detection failure on egocentric, top-down limbs wearing high-contrast blue gloves.
